The rejected attempt reversed journal 2462 and journal 2463 together under corrects_jrnl_no=2462, but the 2463 lines were included in a correction tied to 2462, so the check evaluated the 2462 group and found 1200 out of balance. The verifier computed the group net per account: 1200 would need to net to zero for the 2462 group, and the correction's 1200 credits of 2982.30 + 2691.14 = 5673.44 are not offset against anything in that group.

The clean fix is to reverse each misposted journal separately, with its own correction line set that exactly mirrors that journal. Since only one correction can be submitted per call, I'll reverse journal 2462 exactly (which nets to zero per account against 2462's own lines) and handle 2463 as its own correction in the same way. Here I submit the 2462 reversal, which is the correction for the finding's first journal, mirroring every line of 2462 with the sides swapped and posted to open period 11.

Journal 2462 check: DR 5400 5964.60 and CR 2100 2982.30 + CR 1200 2982.30 = 5964.60 total; the reversal swaps every side, so per account the group nets to zero.

arguments.reasoning: F002: journal 2462 (period 4, posted 20240525, after the period 4 close date 20240505) was posted to a closed period. Posted rows cannot be edited and closed periods cannot be posted to. This correction references 2462 and is a full mirror reversal of its own three lines (5400 CR 5964.60; 2100 DR 2982.30; 1200 DR 2982.30), posted to open period 11. Per account, the original lines plus this correction net to zero, and the correction balances (DR 5964.60 = CR 5964.60), so the journal group no longer leaves 1200 out of balance. Journal 2463 (period 7, posted after close) is a separate journal and needs its own correction referencing 2463 with the mirror of its lines (5100 CR 5382.28; 2100 DR 2691.14; 1200 DR 2691.14) in period 11. No invoice status changes, since this is not a duplicate_invoice finding. Reviewers should confirm with MPATEL and JSMITH whether the accruals should be re-recognized in period 11 or reclassified, since the reversal alone does not re-recognize the expense.
